prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling is a general, ligand-controlled method that replaced harsh classical aryl amination and is now routine in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis. It is original, mature (three decades), independently reproduced everywhere, and it extends the 2010 cross-coupling prize in a way that is chemically distinct (C-N bond formation, ligand design for reductive elimination from amido complexes). Buchwald and Hartwig developed the catalytic systems independently and made the reaction general, which gives a clean two-person attribution. Four members (Aqvist, Somfai, Sparr and I) ranked it, three of us first, so it has the broadest cross-member support on the shortlist.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that it is an incremental extension of a field already honored in 2010, and that Kosugi and Migita's earlier tin-amide work is a genuine precursor whose priority a purist could not dismiss. A second concern is conceptual novelty: ranking it first favors a reliable workhorse over a field that created a new capability, such as targeted protein degradation or base editing.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks C-N coupling first as simple, enabling chemistry with demonstrated consequences, and ranks massively parallel sequencing second, with Rothberg added as a third laureate.
responses.response: I agree on the criterion of demonstrated, general consequence. I would still keep the prize to Buchwald and Hartwig and not add anyone. Adding Kosugi or a third name would blur the clean attribution that is this candidate's main advantage. On sequencing, I see the Solexa chemistry as strong, but the credit is split among Balasubramanian, Klenerman, Mayer, Ju and Rothberg, and I find that harder to resolve than the C-N case.

responses.point: Somfai calls Pd C-N coupling conceptually simple and ligand-controlled, visible in countless syntheses and used at scale, and treats Kosugi's tin-amide work as a precursor.
responses.response: I agree. As a synthetic chemist you are better placed than I am to judge how much Kosugi's work and the Migita-type stannane chemistry anticipated the catalytic cycle. My reading is that his stoichiometric-in-tin chemistry lacked the ligand-enabled generality for amine scope. If you think the priority question is weaker than I do, tell me, because that is the one point that could move me from two names to three.

responses.point: Aili ranks PROTACs first as a new modality that moves pharmacology from occupancy to event-driven degradation, with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli credited.
responses.response: I take the conceptual novelty seriously and ranked it fourth myself. Here I qualify your case. No degrader is approved yet, so the maturity is incomplete, and the attribution is unresolved between the PROTAC concept and the cereblon glue mechanism (Handa, Ito), which a three-person limit cannot cover. I would not oppose it as a later prize, but I do not think it beats a fully mature, cleanly attributed method now.

responses.point: Linke ranks base editing first as a principled new capability with a defined chemical mechanism, crediting Liu, Komor and Gaudelli.
responses.response: I ranked base editing seventh, and I want to explain that. The chemistry (engineered deaminase activity on DNA) is elegant, but I see the case as mainly about Liu's direction of the work, and I am uneasy about crediting the trainee first authors alongside him given the independent Nishida and Kondo work. I would also ask whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as genome engineering that belongs in Medicine. If colleagues convince me that a Liu-only prize is defensible, it moves up for me.

uncertainties: How much weight Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work deserves in attribution, and whether it justifies a third name.
Whether a second extension of the cross-coupling theme so soon after 2010 reads as too incremental for the committee.
Whether the PROTAC case will be mature enough without an approved degrader drug, and how to split credit with the cereblon strand.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. None of the shortlisted candidates is a Stockholm University colleague or a former mentor of mine. My collaboration with Peter Brzezinski is a departmental one only and does not touch these candidates.
